requirement:
`habeas mdbook` MUST NOT require a separate authored coverage chapter or
`{coverage-index}` directive, or use such a directive to control generation
of the subchapter under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
The generated coverage subchapter MUST have no authored source file or edit
target.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.source` that needs implementation evidence.

- "`habeas mdbook` MUST NOT require a separate authored coverage chapter or `{coverage-index}` directive, or use such a directive to control generation" limits what the tool needs from its input. A different implementation could generate the subchapter by any internal mechanism, such as a different builder, data type or function layout. As long as it needs no authored chapter or directive, it still satisfies the clause. The clause names no library, type, signature or delegation.
- "The generated coverage subchapter MUST have no authored source file or edit target" describes the output. An implementation could make this true in many internal ways, and every one of them gives the same observable result. The clause does not say how the chapter is represented.

Both clauses specify behavior only. Test edges exist for this requirement, and I did not assess their adequacy because that belongs to the behavioral criterion. No implementation roots were supplied, and none are needed.

behavioral: Obligations from `requirements.test-coverage.index.source`, and the tests that cover each:

1. `habeas mdbook` MUST NOT require a separate authored coverage chapter or a `{coverage-index}` directive. In `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authored_coverage_directives_do_not_control_generated_placement]`, the first case has only a plain chapter with no directive and no authored coverage chapter. It still asserts that exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" chapter is generated, at `reports/coverage.md`, as the first child of the requirements index. `generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy` also builds books with no authored coverage chapter or directive. It asserts the generated chapter, its numbering, its parent names and its guidance content.

2. The tool MUST NOT use a directive to control generation or placement. The other two cases of `authored_coverage_directives_do_not_control_generated_placement` put one and two `:::{coverage-index}` directives in a different chapter, `elsewhere.md`. They assert that the result is unchanged. There is still exactly one generated chapter, with the same path and parent names, and it is still the child of the requirements index. The authored chapter's content is unchanged and it gets no sub-items, so the directive neither relocates nor duplicates the generated chapter. `generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy` also asserts that the generated content does not contain `:::{coverage-index}`.

3. The generated subchapter MUST have no authored source file or edit target. Both tests assert `source_path.is_none()` for the generated chapter. The hierarchy test asserts the same for its child pages. The directive test also asserts that `md/reports/coverage.md` is not created on disk.

The assertions would fail if generation depended on a directive or an authored chapter, or if the generated chapter had a source path or backing file. I found no unexercised obligation or boundary. Both tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject.
